note: Declarative cross-field consistency rules for the AI System Register (Framework 06, register.py 'validate' command). The engine reads and evaluates these rules; it does not hard-code them. Condition primitives supported: field/op/value comparisons (==, !=, >=, in), empty/populated checks, date_past, in_category (taxonomy category membership), all/any combinators, and the register-wide cross_reference check used by R7.

implementation_notes.R2: Part 1 (section 1.7) requires 'an override-rate evidence field' to be populated for a supports_genuine classification to stand, but the 44-field schema does not name a dedicated override_rate field. This rule uses monitoring_in_place as the closest schema field to that evidence, consistent with Framework 03's control-obligations table, which ties 'override and exception rates' to the monitoring domain. This mapping is a judgement call, not an invented field; see README limitations.
implementation_notes.R8: "vendor does not name a parent product" is operationalised as the vendor field being empty. The schema cannot verify that a populated vendor field actually names a parent product, only that something was recorded.

rules.description: human_oversight_model: in_the_loop with decision_role: makes is internally contradictory (section 1.9)
decision_role: supports_genuine with no override-rate evidence field populated, see section 1.7 evidence test
affects_people: external_individuals and decision_role in (makes, supports_determinative) and no Layer 3 populated, probable registration trigger
lifecycle_status: in_use and next_review_due in the past, stale
autonomy_level >= 4 and human_oversight_model: none and affects_people != no, escalate
depends_on references a system_id not in the register, broken dependency
provenance: embedded_feature and vendor does not name a parent product
system_type in agentic category and no systems_integrated recorded, action scope unknown
lifecycle_status: in_trial and no risk_tier, pilots are not exempt, section 1.8
